title: Prove the extraction changed nothing
description:
Re-derive and re-score against the frozen baseline. Identical output, or the extraction is wrong and gets reverted rather than patched.

This is the gate the whole project's evidence depends on: every number in FINDINGS was produced by the pre-move code.
acceptance_criteria: Re-scored dev and held-out match the baseline exactly; dev is 3.76s/0.51s for t3 as it is today; any difference blocks the merge.

title: Freeze the current results as the extraction baseline
description: Before moving any code: capture the scored output of every stored config so the move can be proved identical. data/results.jsonl already holds it; snapshot the derived segments per config too, since rederive.py rewrites them in place.
acceptance_criteria: A committed baseline file covering all 181 stored results; a one-command comparison that reports any drift.

title: Move the library modules, no other change
description: audio, blocks, cues, segments, rules, features, acoustic, the render chain, the ollama client. Imports updated, nothing else touched — no renames, no comment cleanup, no refactoring. The argparse drivers stay in experiments/ and are left frozen.
acceptance_criteria: Every moved module imports from src/sermon/pipeline; experiments/ still runs; the diff contains only moves and import lines.

title: pytest-bdd harness over features/
description:
Point pytest-bdd at features/ so all 460 scenarios collect and fail as undefined rather than erroring. Register the spec tags as pytest marks (they warn otherwise). Wire features/validate_spec.py in as a test so the spec cannot silently stop parsing.

Verified already: the whole spec collects as 604 tests.
acceptance_criteria: `pytest --collect-only` reports 604 tests, 0 errors; validate_spec passes as a test; ADR-LS-001 Red phase is genuine (undefined, not error).
close_reason: pytest-bdd collects all 604 scenarios with no hand-maintained list; 17 spec tags registered as marks; validate_spec wired in as a test. Two review rounds closed nine execution-verified routes by which the suite could go green while the spec was silenced, hollowed or partly unread — spec size, step count (1898), executed-vs-skipped counts, deferral level, recursive step discovery, and hooks refused in step modules are each pinned by a guard test.

title: Extract the validated pipeline into the package
description:
experiments/src mixes library code with argparse CLI drivers. The product wants the library half.

Highest-risk task in the project: every number in FINDINGS rests on this code. The move must be provably behaviour-preserving and must NOT be combined with refactoring or comment cleanup.

title: Per-approval distribution consent is not recorded anywhere
description: interface/segment_review.feature, Rule 'I am told whose voice this is before I publish it': when a Segment's teaching voice matches no enrolled profile and its intent is publish, the reviewer is asked to confirm the recording may be distributed, and 'the confirmation is recorded with the approval'. No DOMAIN.md field records that per-Segment consent. SpeakerProfile.confirmed_by_human is about the profile, not about this approval. The scenario's own comment calls this 'the one place the system can cause real harm: a guest preacher who asked not to be distributed, approved ten days later by a reviewer who has forgotten' -- so the safeguard is exactly the thing the domain model does not store.
acceptance_criteria: The approval records the distribution confirmation, and the store persists it.

title: Segment has no Date or Label field, but the render filename needs both
description: interface/publication_details.feature requires a Date and a Label saved with the Segment -- the output MP3 filename is built from them, matching the corpus convention '2026-09-13 - Hebrews 12.25-29.mp3'. DOMAIN.md's Segment section has no field for either. This blocks the render naming rules in processing, and is the largest of the domain gaps found while building the store.
acceptance_criteria: DOMAIN.md's Segment carries the publication date and label, and the store persists them.

title: Notification is fully specified but absent from DOMAIN.md
description: features/notifications/approval_notifications.feature specifies a Notification entity with an explicit field table (subject, kind, recipient, summary, created_at, state) and four states (pending, delivered, failed, suppressed), under the Rule 'A Notification is a record, not a message'. DOMAIN.md models seven entities and does not mention it, and its 'What this model deliberately does not decide' section does not list it either -- so this is an omission, not a decision. analysis_orchestration.feature also promises 'a notification is sent to the reviewers unless nothing publishable was found'. Consequence: the store built in sp-1vn.3 cannot persist a Notification, and the notifications feature file cannot be implemented until the entity exists. Verified: zero mentions of 'notification' in DOMAIN.md; state values 'suppressed' and 'failed' appear in features/ but in no DOMAIN.md or README table.
acceptance_criteria: DOMAIN.md models Notification with every field its feature file's table names, and the store persists it with its states closed.

title: Integrity check: do step definitions assert what the Gherkin says?
description:
Recurring guard against the failure this whole arrangement exists to prevent: a suite that goes green while meaning nothing. Sample the scenarios implemented since the last integrity check, read each against its step definitions, and ask only whether the assertion is as strong as the Gherkin. A step that passes while testing something weaker is an IMPORTANT finding and becomes a bead.

Re-open and re-run this every ten bead closures. Do not close it permanently.
acceptance_criteria: A named sample of at least 8 implemented scenarios reviewed; for each, a verdict on whether its step definitions assert the full Gherkin; every weakening filed as a bead; the sample and verdicts recorded in the close reason.
notes: Deferred so it is not picked up before there is anything to check. The loop re-opens it (bd update sp-dzc --defer=none) after every ten bead closures.

title: Store: entities from DOMAIN.md
description: SQLite schema and access layer for Recording, Block, Segment, Proposal, Artifact, Job, SpeakerProfile. Every field in features/DOMAIN.md cites the behaviour that forces it; a field with no scenario behind it does not get built.
acceptance_criteria: Each entity round-trips; the state columns accept only the values in README.md's lifecycle tables; artifact paths resolve under the configured data root.
close_reason: SQLite store for the seven DOMAIN.md entities: generated DDL, 12 closed sets derived from README.md's own tables with CHECK enforcement, ordered child collections, data-root-relative paths guarded on write and resolvable on read. Review found a data-integrity defect — saves() never rolled back, so a refused row became durable on the next successful write — plus five Important findings; all fixed and pinned by regression tests that assert a refusal left no row, checked through a second connection.

title: Package skeleton and pyproject
description: src/sermon/ with pipeline, web, jobs, store subpackages per ARCHITECTURE.md. pyproject with the verified dependency set: faster-whisper 1.2.1, sherpa-onnx 1.13.8, numpy, flask, pytest-bdd 8.1.0, playwright 1.63.0.
acceptance_criteria: `pip install -e .` succeeds; `import sermon` works; no module imports from experiments/.
close_reason: src/sermon package skeleton with pipeline/web/jobs/store, pyproject with verified pins, and an import-hygiene test that catches sys.path routes into experiments/ as well as static imports

title: Foundations: package, container, store
description:
Project scaffold that everything else needs. Python package layout per ARCHITECTURE.md, a single-stage Dockerfile with ffmpeg, the SQLite store and the entities in features/DOMAIN.md, and the pytest-bdd harness wired to features/ so scenarios can start failing for the right reason.

No feature file governs this directly; DOMAIN.md and ARCHITECTURE.md do.

title: Proposal is 1:1 but the spec requires proposal history
description: DOMAIN.md makes Proposal one per Segment, replaced when analysis re-runs. analysis_orchestration.feature requires two things a 1:1 cannot express: 'the previous Proposals are kept in the Recording's history' when analysis is re-run, and 'the new machine proposal is shown alongside it as a suggestion' when a reviewer has already edited a Segment's boundaries. The same file also promises 'the retry is visible in the Recording's processing log', and there is no log entity. Either Proposal becomes 1:N with a supersession chain (Artifact already has superseded_by as precedent) or the scenarios are wrong.
acceptance_criteria: Proposal history and the processing log are either modelled or the scenarios are changed to match.

title: Speaker match confidence has nowhere to live
description: interface/segment_review.feature promises 'I am told which enrolled voice is teaching, and how confidently', and that an unrecognised voice shows as 'not a known voice'. DOMAIN.md's SpeakerProfile-to-Block relationship is a bare N:M with no match-confidence field, so the store can record that a voice was recognised but not how strongly. That scenario is tagged @measured -- identification was measured at 4 of 4 leave-one-out -- so the number exists and simply has no home.
acceptance_criteria: The speaker-to-block link carries a match confidence, and the store round-trips it.

title: DOMAIN.md says eleven Recording states; README lists ten
description: DOMAIN.md:52 says Recording state is 'One of eleven. See the lifecycle in README.md'. README.md's lifecycle table lists ten Recording rows: discovered, downloading, ingest_failed, downloaded, analyzing, analysis_failed, ignored, awaiting_review, reviewed, discarded. Verified independently: 10 rows, and every Recording state string used anywhere in features/ falls within those ten, so the table is not missing one that the spec uses. The store was built with ten because the sp-1vn.3 acceptance criterion names README's table as the authority. DOMAIN.md is most likely just stale -- but one of the two documents is wrong and a reader cannot tell which. sp-1vn.3's bead description inherited the same wrong count.
acceptance_criteria: The two documents agree, and the store's closed set matches.

title: validate_spec counts scenarios by regex, so its summary line can be forged
description: features/validate_spec.py:84 derives its scenario and rule counts from a line regex over raw text rather than from the Gherkin parse tree it already builds. The harness now pins the summary string 'spec OK - 34 files, 460 scenarios, 142 rules', so a forgeable count weakens that guard. Executed during review: deleting a real scenario, adding one Examples row elsewhere, and adding a 'Scenario: not a real scenario' line inside a Gherkin docstring together kept the summary at 460 scenarios and 604 collected with all guard tests green, while the spec was genuinely one scenario lighter. A single fake docstring line alone moves the count to 461. Three coordinated edits is contrived rather than a likely accident, which is why this is not urgent -- but the pinned string is weaker than it looks until the counts come from the AST.
acceptance_criteria: Scenario and rule counts come from the parse tree; a fake Scenario line inside a docstring does not change them.

title: Homelab end-to-end benchmark
description: Run one recording through the full pipeline on nas. Every performance figure in FINDINGS is from a laptop. Deferred: the owner asked for this to wait until the box is idle, and it is also a possible purchasing decision.
acceptance_criteria: A three-hour recording transcribed, diarized, classified and rendered on nas, with wall-clock per stage recorded in FINDINGS.

Every bead: acceptance criteria drawn from its own scenarios rather than invented; named governing feature file and Rule; dependencies only within this phase or on closed work. title: Path resolution collapses .. textually rather than resolving it
description: artifact_paths.py uses os.path.normpath, so 'link/../secret.txt' where link is a symlink out of the data root is rewritten to root/secret.txt instead of being resolved POSIX-style. The result is safely inside the root -- it just names a different file than the caller wrote. Separately, a path containing a NUL byte raises a bare ValueError from lstat rather than PathEscapesDataRoot; both are ValueError, so a caller catching the base class is unaffected. Found while attacking the guard with 25 inputs, all of which stayed inside the root.
acceptance_criteria: Path resolution matches POSIX semantics, and every refusal raises the store's own error type.

title: A stale database schema is silently accepted
description: opens_store executescripts CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so an existing database with an older schema is accepted and then fails later with an OperationalError at the first query touching a new column. Omitting a migration framework is right at 39 recordings and ~1/week, but the silence could be made loud with a schema-hash check at open.
acceptance_criteria: A database whose schema does not match the code is reported at open, not at first query.

title: Store helper names depart from the naming rule
description: close() is the one Store method that is not a third-person singular verb phrase, alongside saves/loads/lists/resolves. Several module helpers are noun phrases too: order_by, to_column, from_column, values_of, column_names. CONVENTIONS.md keeps LS-003's naming rule even though the Rails-scoped ADR itself does not apply here.
acceptance_criteria: Names are third-person singular verb phrases.

title: A NaN in a REAL column silently becomes 'not measured'
description: float('nan') stored in a REAL column comes back as None, turning 'measured and degenerate' into 'never measured'. This matters for the emptiness-gate fields dynamic_range_db, active_fraction and longest_active_seconds, where that distinction decides whether a recording is treated as empty.
acceptance_criteria: A degenerate measurement is distinguishable from an absent one.

title: The store has no single-row sanity constraints
description: Accepted without complaint: Block(start=500, end=10), Segment(punch_in=900, punch_out=10), negative timecodes, Job(attempts=-5, max_attempts=0), an Artifact whose superseded_by is itself, and a Segment on recording r2 seeded by a Block belonging to r1. Multi-row block contiguity genuinely cannot be a CHECK, but every case above can. Deliberately out of scope for sp-1vn.3, whose criteria named only the closed sets.
acceptance_criteria: Single-row invariants a CHECK can express are enforced.

title: The DDL generator does not escape SQL string literals
description: quoted() in src/sermon/store/schema.py emits 'it''s' incorrectly as 'it's' for a value containing an apostrophe. Unexploitable today -- no vocabulary value contains one, and all 12 sets are derived from the spec's own tables -- but the generator has no defence if one ever does.
acceptance_criteria: Values are escaped, or a value that cannot be safely quoted fails loudly.

title: Collection links silently keep duplicates
description: Link tables key on (owner, position), so enrolled_from=('r1','r1') round-trips unchanged and one speaker_profile_id can be linked to the same block twice. DOMAIN.md:165 describes enrolled_from as 'Which Recordings contributed. Needed to un-enrol', which reads as a set.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate links are refused or deduplicated, per what the spec implies.

title: The speaker N:M link is navigable in only one direction
description: DOMAIN.md:32 draws SpeakerProfile -> Block, but lists(Block, speaker_profile_ids=...) and lists(SpeakerProfile, enrolled_from=...) both raise ValueError because column_names() excludes collection fields. The link round-trips from the Block side, so the relationship exists, but profile -> blocks needs raw SQL. segment_review.feature asks which enrolled voice is teaching (the Block-side question); the reverse direction is what un-enrolling a speaker needs.
acceptance_criteria: Both directions of the link are queryable through the store.

title: DOMAIN.md writes Block evidence as a scalar but the spec asserts several
description: DOMAIN.md:78 writes Block's evidence unbracketed while DOMAIN.md:118 writes Proposal's as evidence[]. analysis/block_classification.feature:165-166 asserts two evidence entries on a single Block ('sustained single-speaker teaching' AND 'follows a scripture reading') and :90 says each Block carries the evidence that produced it -- so the plural is correct and DOMAIN.md's wording misleads. The store was changed to an ordered child table under sp-1vn.3; this is the documentation half.
acceptance_criteria: DOMAIN.md writes Block evidence as a collection.

title: Job.job_id is the one surrogate id no scenario forces
description: Job.job_id was added as a row identity, but nothing in DOMAIN.md references a job identity -- unlike seed_block_id, segment_id, superseded_by and speaker_profile_id, which the N:M link needs. dedupe_key is already UNIQUE and could serve. Defensible as a row identity, but it is the one addition the sp-1vn.3 rule 'a field with no scenario behind it does not get built' does not cover.
acceptance_criteria: Either a forcing behaviour is cited for job_id, or it is removed.

title: Recording.kind is nullable while the vocabulary already has 'unknown'
description: RECORDING_KINDS contains 'unknown' (README.md:96) and Recording.kind is also nullable, so there are two encodings of one fact. DOMAIN.md:53 flags no nullability for the field. Pick one.
acceptance_criteria: A recording of unknown kind has exactly one representation.

title: Source-no-longer-available flags have no fields
description: operations/storage_and_retention.feature requires that a Recording can be flagged 'source no longer available' and that its skipped Segments are marked as no longer extractable. DOMAIN.md has no field for either. Related but distinct from the open Q34 question about whether local audio is ever reclaimed, which DOMAIN.md does list as deliberately undecided.
acceptance_criteria: Both flags exist in DOMAIN.md and the store, or the scenarios are changed.

title: validate_spec docstring names the out-of-range interpreter
description: features/validate_spec.py:9 still says to run it from features/ as 'python3 validate_spec.py'. python3 on PATH is 3.14.3, outside the >=3.13,<3.14 pyproject declares, and that command exits 2 with 'gherkin-official is not installed'. CLAUDE.md was corrected to .venv/bin/python features/validate_spec.py; this docstring now contradicts it. The script itself is cwd-independent (Path(__file__).parent), so the instruction is merely stale.
acceptance_criteria: The docstring names a command that runs.

title: Size test spawns a redundant collect-only subprocess
description: tests/test_spec_harness.py:76 test_the_spec_is_the_size_this_harness_was_built_for runs a --collect-only subprocess identical to the one test_the_spec_module_collects_every_declared_scenario already runs. Harmless at this size; the count could be shared through a session fixture.
acceptance_criteria: The collection count is obtained once per session.

title: A step module's plural name describes a single-module operation
description: tests/conftest.py:11 loads_step_definitions loads and returns exactly one module from one path; the plural reads as the whole-directory operation, which is pytest_configure. loads_step_module or loads_step_definitions_from would match. The third-person singular verb form is already correct per CONVENTIONS.md.
acceptance_criteria: The name describes what the function does.

title: features/README declares two tags no scenario uses
description: The tag table in features/README.md declares @needs-decision and @mobile, which no scenario carries. validate_spec.py enforces the dangerous direction only (every tag used must be declared), so this passes. @needs-decision is expected to be empty -- all spec decisions are settled -- but @mobile is suspicious: interface/segment_review.feature has a Rule about mobile review that carries no such tag. Decide whether the tag or the table is wrong.
acceptance_criteria: Either the tags are used, or they are removed from the table, with the mobile scenarios' tagging decided deliberately.

title: gherkin-official floods every run with 4040 DeprecationWarnings
description: A full suite run emits ~4040 DeprecationWarnings from inside gherkin-official==29.0.0 (gherkin_line.py:79, maxsplit passed positionally). 808 arise from pytest-bdd's own parse, so they appear on every run regardless of the harness tests. Harmless, but they bury any real warning, which matters because the harness relies on warnings-as-errors to catch unknown marks. No filter was added in sp-1vn.2 deliberately, to avoid masking anything.
acceptance_criteria: A clean run's warning output is readable: the dependency is bumped, or the warning is filtered narrowly enough that a new warning from our own code still surfaces.

title: Nothing tests that the spec guardrail still detects anything
description: Neutering validate_spec.main() to return 0 leaves all harness tests green: the guardrail is wired in, but its ability to detect a regression is untested. It is demonstrably live today -- planting forbidden implementation vocabulary in a scenario and adding an undeclared tag each fail the suite -- so this is a latent hole rather than a present one.
acceptance_criteria: A test fails if validate_spec stops detecting a known-bad spec.

title: Spec roots and marker descriptions are duplicated
description: PROJECT_ROOT/SPEC_ROOT are defined three times (tests/test_spec_harness.py:9, tests/conftest.py:6, tests/test_spec.py:5). Separately, the 17 marker descriptions in pyproject.toml duplicate features/README.md's table prose while the test compares only names, so the descriptions can drift from the table unnoticed.
acceptance_criteria: The roots have one definition; either the descriptions are compared too or they stop being duplicated.

title: Six scenario names collide across feature files
description: Collecting all 604 scenarios in one module collapses six duplicate scenario names to _1 suffixes -- e.g. 'A quiet margin around the cut' in analysis/punch_in_detection.feature:39 and analysis/punch_out_detection.feature:76, and 'Both channels carry signal' in analysis/audio_probe.feature:40 and processing/audio_rendering.feature:30. No scenario is lost (604 == 604) and the suffix survived a file rename, but test_a_quiet_margin_around_the_cut_1 no longer says which feature file it came from, and a step definition written for punch-in will be matched against punch-out. The collision is in features/; renaming scenarios is a spec edit and must keep validate_spec.py passing.
acceptance_criteria: Scenario names are unique across the spec, or node ids carry their feature file.

title: Deferred-tag hook reimplements pytest-bdd's own default
description: tests/conftest.py:23 applies pytest.mark.deferred(function) and discards the return value, relying on in-place mutation. It duplicates what pytest-bdd's default pytest_bdd_apply_tag already does. Applying only skip and returning None lets the default apply the mark, and is shorter.
acceptance_criteria: The hook applies only what pytest-bdd does not, and does not rely on a discarded return value.

title: Harness helpers are noun phrases, against LS-003 naming
description: CONVENTIONS.md LS-003 keeps the naming rule: one operation per unit, named as a third-person singular verb phrase. In tests/test_spec_harness.py, runs_pytest complies; counted (:24), tag_names (:30), expanded_scenarios (:34) and declared_scenarios (:49) do not. Four against one in a 110-line file.
acceptance_criteria: Helper names are third-person singular verb phrases.

title: Marker registration is asserted from pyproject, not from effective pytest config
description: tests/test_spec_harness.py:80 reads pyproject.toml's file content via tomllib rather than pytest's resolved configuration. Adding a pytest.ini shadowed all 17 marker registrations, producing 15 PytestUnknownMarkWarning, and this test still passed. Only test_no_tag_the_spec_uses_is_an_unknown_mark caught it, and that one structurally cannot cover the two declared-but-unused tags (@mobile, @needs-decision).
acceptance_criteria: The test reads pytest's effective markers so a shadowing config file fails the suite.

title: Harness test discards a return code it should check
description: tests/test_spec_harness.py:64 calls runs_pytest(...)[1] and throws away the second run's return code, so the expected total is computed from an unchecked baseline. The primary run's returncode still catches a collection error, so this is cosmetic rather than a live hole.
acceptance_criteria: Both return codes are checked, or the second run is removed.

title: Decompose Operations and notifications into per-Rule beads

Every bead: acceptance criteria drawn from its own scenarios rather than invented; named governing feature file and Rule; dependencies only within this phase or on closed work. Cross-cutting concepts are named and handled deliberately rather than sliced per-Rule. bd ready after the change offers only beads whose dependencies are genuinely satisfiable.

acceptance_criteria: tests/ and services/ are scanned by the same assertions that cover src/.

title: Clean comments to the LS-004 bar, separately

Dedicated commit after the move is proved identical, never combined with it — ADR-LS-004 section 7.

Outstanding on adoption: 18 comment blocks over the three-line ceiling, 9 carrying dates, 5 first person, 5.5% density. Most duplicate FINDINGS, which is where rationale belongs.

title: Deploy to nas
